summary: Prioritize immediate 'counter-intuitive' claims in the first sentence; high-stayed videos debunk common assumptions rather than just asking questions.
Eliminate 'Ever noticed' or 'How X works' openers; these produce the lowest stayed_pct (25-37%) because they feel like slow introductions.
Use titles that frame the topic as a secret or a conflict (e.g., 'eating you back', 'secretly leaking') rather than a neutral educational prompt.
Keep the hook under 15 words; videos with concise, punchy first sentences achieved a minimum 50% stayed_pct.
Avoid countdowns or generic 'thought' emojis in titles, as they correlate with the bottom-performing videos in this dataset.
winning_hooks: Your fingers prune in water, but it is not because you are absorbing it like a sponge.
Your eyes are leaking right now, and your brain is hiding it.
Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back.
This shark is older than the United States.
avoid: Starting with a question ('Ever noticed...?', 'Why do...?')
Slow, descriptive openers that explain the context before the hook.
next_experiment: Create two versions of the same topic: Version A starts with an immediate, counter-intuitive statement (e.g., 'You are holding a parasite right now'), and Version B starts with a question (e.g., 'Do you know why you have this in your hand?'), measuring the difference in stayed_pct.
